hints.content:
We can map a figure onto a **similar** figure using only rigid transformations and dilations. This means the figures must have exactly the same shapes, but may have different sizes.

For triangles in particular, two triangles are similar if all of their corresponding angles are [[☃ definition 1]].

options.definition: Angles with the same measure that we can map onto each other using rigid transformations

hints.content:
Triangle $ABC$ has angle measures of $47^\circ$ and $86^\circ$. The third angle measure is therefore $180^\circ - 47^\circ - 86^\circ = 47^\circ$.



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: Triangle A B C. Angle A is eighty-six degrees. Angle B is forty-seven degrees. Angle C is forty-seven degrees.

hints.content:
Triangle $MPN$ has angle measures of $47^\circ$ and $47^\circ$. The third angle measure is $180^\circ - 47^\circ - 47^\circ = 86^\circ$.



[[☃ image 1]]

Therefore $\triangle MPN$ is similar to $\triangle ABC$.

options.alt: Triangle M N P. Angle M is eighty-six degrees. Angle P is forty-seven degrees. Angle N is forty-seven degrees.

hints.content:
Triangle $QRS$ has angle measures of $47^\circ$ and $47^\circ$. The third angle measure is $180^\circ - 47^\circ - 47^\circ = 86^\circ$.



[[☃ image 1]]

Therefore $\triangle QRS$ is similar to $\triangle ABC$.

options.alt: Triangle Q R S. Angle Q is eighty-six degrees. Angle R is forty-seven degrees. Angle S is forty-seven degrees.

hints.content: In conclusion, *both* triangles are similar to $\triangle ABC$.
